mint.1:28:
```mezze
effect Async where {
  spawn: { f: {} -> 'a } -> Promise 'a
}
```

---

Unified async effect for spawning, awaiting, and structured concurrency.

The effect carries only the primitives that a handler must implement.
The Async effect declares a single primitive: `spawn`. Every other
async operation (`await`, `cancel`, `sleep`, `yield_now`, `park`,
`scoped`) lives as a stdlib free function above, either delegating
to a native or riding on another effect (Time). Derived operations
(race, all, any, settle, join, join3, par_map, par_for_each,
par_filter, with_timeout, try_*) live as free functions below —
each expressible in terms of `spawn` + the primitives.

This keeps the ability surface minimal: implementers pick a
scheduler (Loom vs OS threads), everything else composes on top.

Cancellation observation is Promise-side (`p.is_cancelled {}`);
delivery inside a task rides on the JDK's blocking-primitive
interrupt (sleep, await, park, mutex/channel/latch waits are all
cancellation points). Pure CPU-bound tasks are not interruptible
by design — sprinkle a natural yield point (await, sleep, or the
like) if you need cooperative cancel.
